checked_sources: Independent replay for each counterexample row with selected probabilities (a,b): maximize 1, 2(1−b)+|2b−1|, 2(1−a)+2a(1−b)+|2ab−1|, and 2(1−a)+2(1−a)(1−b)+|1−2b(1−a)|. These correspond to the four ancestral sign choices.
correctness.rationale: Fix an evaluation leaf. Multiplying the signed kernel by the current path mass gives state t; a normalized Haar product across the next two children is minus the inverse parent mass. Thus the omitted sibling contributes (1−p)|t−e| to the absolute row integral and the new state is pt+(1−p)e; the final leaf contributes |t_d|. Every state lies in [−1,1], and the finite operator norm is exactly the maximum absolute row integral. Changing a selected p to q≥p decreases the current term by (q−p)|t−e| while moving the next state by the same distance. With suffix signs fixed, its Lipschitz coefficients telescope to one, so the row cannot increase; maximizing over signs preserves this comparison. For r≤1/2, substitution into the suffix value A+B|t| reduces maximization to choosing the sign opposite to t since (1−r)−rB≥0 for 0≤B≤1. This gives the recurrence and the sharp upper envelope, attained on a consistent minority path of the homogeneous tree. Fair splits give B=1/3+(2/3)(−1/2)^k with k remaining splits, and summing yields F_d. A one-level defect shifts A and B at level j by (1+B_{j+1})δ; through the earlier fair levels the B shift gains successive factors −1/2 and the A increments are half of the incoming B shift. Summing gives precisely C_{d,j}δ. A path through the largest first bias can take all subsequent minority children; monotonicity compares it with the isolated defect. For a single biased node the other paths are fair or take its majority child and cannot exceed the defect value. This proves uniqueness of the fair minimum including depth one. The four two-step rows give 5/2, 5/2, 27/10, and 11/10, so the unique norming leaf is majority-first.
residual_risks: The finite rational diagnostics are not universal certificates; the row comparison and finite-depth induction prove the stated real-probability claims. The upper envelope is attainable over the class, not necessarily for a given heterogeneous tree. The result uses full finite binary generations and real signs, including the constant coefficient.

value.rationale: A sharp comparison usable with only the minimal child probabilities on each generation controls a natural endpoint norm without enumerating all signs or evaluating every leaf. The first-bias coefficient gives a quantitative, attained rigidity statement that the fair endpoint value alone cannot give. The small greedy counterexample clarifies what the comparison does not compute for an individual tree, rather than serving as an isolated curiosity.
residual_risks: The result does not classify every heterogeneous norming leaf, suppressions, nonbinary or ragged biased trees, or arbitrary complex phases.
